title: Anthropic Launches Claude Personal Finance Feature, Supporting Smart Spending Analysis and Bill Tracking

content_html:
On November 5 local time, AI company Anthropic announced the official launch of a new Personal Finance feature for Claude, with a limited rollout beginning this week for Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the United States. The launch of this new feature marks that large models are gradually moving beyond acting merely as office and creative assistants and are increasingly penetrating users' everyday financial and life management scenarios.

Clarify your financial situation with natural language, with a focus on absolute security and objectivity

In the past, if users wanted to fully understand their monthly spending, they often had to open different banking apps one by one, export statements, and calculate everything manually. With Claude's new personal finance feature, users only need to securely link their bank accounts and can then talk directly with the AI in natural language.

To ease users' concerns about the safety of their funds, the company explicitly emphasizes that this feature has read-only access. This means Claude absolutely cannot transfer or manage users' funds, let alone make any investment decisions on their behalf. At the same time, consistent with Claude's long-standing product positioning, the personal finance section has no ads and will not push any commercially sponsored recommendations; because Anthropic itself does not issue credit cards, offer loans, or provide its own savings accounts, the financial answers users receive from the AI remain highly objective and direct.

Context-aware intelligent analysis: from checking balances to uncovering hidden bills

To give readers a more intuitive understanding of how it works in practice, the company demonstrated several typical everyday scenarios:

Detailed spending summaries: Suppose payday is still 10 days away, and the user asks Claude, "Where did all my money go this month?" The system will automatically summarize spending across all linked accounts and provide a clear, categorized breakdown.

Alerts for unusual bills and hidden fees: When users ask whether there are any unusual bills, Claude will thoroughly scan all linked accounts and help them notice easily overlooked details, such as duplicate charges, unexplained fees, or subscription bills that quietly increased in price over the course of a year.

Big-picture financial Q&A and term explanations: Users can also ask broader, more macro-level questions, such as "Is my spending already more than my income?" or "What is APR, and how much interest did it cost me this year?" The system will first explain financial terms in plain language, then precisely calculate the total amount of interest the user actually incurred.

Customized data dashboards: In addition, users can request weekly spending charts, a calendar of upcoming bills, or custom data dashboards based on their personal needs, and can adjust them at any time after they are generated.

Official risk notice: data can be verified, but no investment advice is provided

When releasing the feature, Anthropic again emphasized that the core purpose of the personal finance feature is to help users understand their financial situation, and that it does not provide any investment advice.

Given that large models may still make errors when processing data, the company recommends that when users review analysis results, they can ask Claude at any time to list the specific transactions behind the corresponding data. If important amounts are involved, they should be sure to verify them against the bank's official data.
